signal sigOut : integer; begin ints1 : entity work.leaf port map( sigInt,sigOut); process begin sigInt <= 10; wait for 1 ns; report "sigOut=" & to_string(sigOut); wait; end process; end architecture; The following are the commands to run the test case: % vhdlan -vhdl08 -q test.vhd % vcs ent -q % simv -q Output Report NOTE at 1 NS in design unit ENT(ARCH) from process /ENT/_P0: "sigOut=1" (simv): Simulation complete, time is 1 NS.
```

## Support for Static Composite Expressions

VCS provides additional support for the use of locally static expressions as defined in VHDL 2008 LRM, Section 9.4 . A locally static expression can be of a composite type, if the subtype of each of the primaries in the expression is locally static and has a locally static subtype.

VCS expands the support for the following kinds of locally static expressions:

- Composite types, such as arrays and records.
- Allowed primaries in a locally expression can be array or record aggregates, indexed array elements, array slices, selected record elements and so on.
- The operators in an expression can either be any of the predefined operators or functions or those defined in the standard packages, such as std\_logic\_1164 , numeric\_bit , numeric\_std , numeric\_bit\_unsigned , and numeric\_std\_unsigned .

## Usage Examples

The following examples show the use of static composite expressions in case and select statements:

## Use of Case Choice and Constant Initializations

## Example 249 Usage of case choice and constant initializations

```
library ieee; use ieee.std_logic_1164.all; use ieee.numeric_std.all; entity e is port( p1:in bit_vector(3 downto 0); p2:in std_logic_vector(3 downto 0); p3:in unsigned(3 downto 0)); end entity; architecture arch_e of e is constant kbv1:bit_vector(3 downto 0):=(others => '0'); constant kbv2:bit_vector(3 downto 0):='0'&(kbv1(2 downto 0) xor "001"); constant kst1:std_logic_vector(3 downto 0):=(others => '0'); constant kst2:std_logic_vector(2 downto 0):=To_StdULogicVector(kbv2(2 downto 0)); constant kun1:unsigned(2 downto 0):=(others => '0'); constant kun2:unsigned(3 downto 0):=resize(unsigned'("10"),4); constant kun3:unsigned(3 downto 0):=SHIFT_RIGHT("1010",1); begin -- predefined types bit-vector process(p1)begin case(p1)is when kbv1                              => report "p1:bit_vector value is 0"; -- 0000 when "00"&"01"                         => report "p1:bit_vector value is 1"; -- 0001 when ("0001" sll 1)                    => report "p1:bit_vector value is 2"; -- 0010 when ("0111" and "1011")               => report "p1:bit_vector value is 3"; -- 0011 when kbv2(1 downto 0)&"00"             => report "p1:bit_vector value is 4"; -- 0100 when (2=>kbv2(0),0=>'1',others=>'0')   => report "p1:bit_vector value is 5"; -- 0101 when others                            => report "p1:bit_vector value is unknown"; end case; end process; -- std_logic_vector
```

## Use of Select Choice and Constant Initialization

## Example 250 Usage of select choice and constant initialization

## Limitations

The following are the limitations for the static composite expression feature:

- Complete packages of numeric\_bit and numeric\_bit\_unsigned are not supported.
- The following function calls from numeric\_std and numeric\_std\_unsigned packages are not supported:
- minimum and maximum
- find\_leftmost and find\_rightmost
- to\_string and similar string conversions
- resize function with vector size is not supported but only scalar size is supported.
- The string conversion function to\_string and similar string conversions present in the std\_logic\_1164 package are not supported.
- Only 'ascending , 'left , 'right , 'low , 'high , 'length , and 'range attributes are supported.
- Aggregated and index selects from multidimensional arrays are not supported.
- The physical data types are not supported.
- Using aliased objects to slices of vectors is not supported.

## Support for VHDL 2008 Enhanced Generics in Components

VCS supports the usage of VHDL 2008 enhanced generics (types/subprograms/ packages) in components and corresponding instantiations of components with generic maps as defined in the VHDL 2008 LRM.

With this support of enhanced generics in VHDL 2008, you can declare generic types, sub-programs, and packages in a component. This allows you to declare abstract and reusable entities with different types and design specialization. When you instantiate a component, you supply values for the generic constants for that instance.

## Following is the use model to enable this feature:

```
% vhdlan -vhdl08 <other_options> file.vhd
```

<!-- image -->

## Examples

The following example shows the usage of generic type and function in component interface:

## Example 251 test.vhd

```
entity GenericCnt is generic ( type T; Constant C : T; function GenFunc (signal arg : T) return T ); port ( clk : in bit; rst : in bit; Cnt : inout T ); end; architecture arch of GenericCnt is begin process(clk,rst) begin if(rst='1') then cnt <= C; elsif(clk'event and clk='1') then cnt <= GenFunc(cnt); end if; end process; end architecture arch; library ieee; use ieee.std_logic_1164.all; use ieee.std_logic_unsigned.all; use ieee.std_logic_arith.all; entity top is end entity; architecture arch of top is component GenericCnt is generic ( type T; Constant C : T; function GenFunc(signal arg : T) return T ); port ( clk : in bit; rst : in bit; Cnt : inout T );
```

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

```
end component; signal clk , rst : bit; signal cnt : std_logic_vector(2 downto 0):= (others => '0'); function IncrCnt ( signal arg : in std_logic_vector ) return std_logic_vector is begin return arg + 1; end function; begin inst : GenericCnt generic map( T => std_logic_vector(2 downto 0), C => (others => '0'), GenFunc => IncrCnt ) port map ( clk,rst,cnt); process begin if(now = 80 ns) then wait; else clk <= '0'; wait for 5 ns; clk <= '1'; wait for 5 ns; end if; end process; process begin rst <= '1'; wait for 3 ns; rst <= '0'; wait for 10 ns; wait; end process; process(cnt) use std.textio.all; use ieee.std_logic_textio.all; variable l : line; begin write(l,"time : " & time'image(now)); write(l," CNT : " & integer'image(conv_integer(unsigned(cnt)))); writeline(output,l); end process; end architecture;
```

```
configuration c of e is for a end for; end configuration;
```

## Limitations

The following are the limitations of the VHDL 2008 Enhanced Generics in Components feature:

- Component with enhanced generics can be configured in the configuration declaration with just entity aspect, which is the common case, like:

```
for u1:l use entity l; end for;
```

The limitation is that the incremental generic or port map is not supported.

## Note:

This limitation is only for configuration declaration. Components with enhanced generics can be fully configured in configuration specifications, including incremental generic or port map.

```

## Support for VHDL 2008 Local Packages

The front-end and back-end compilers of VCS support the VHDL 2008 Local Packages feature. You must use the -vhdl08 option for the VHDL 2008 feature.

<!-- image -->

## Use either of the following methods to enable the VHDL 2008 Local Packages feature:

- Use the -Xlocal\_pack vhdlan option.
- Specify LOCAL\_PACK=TRUE in the synopsys\_sim.setup file.

## Example 254 Global uninstantiated package, multiple local package instantiation

```
package gp i generic(type t; n : t); function f return t; end package; package body gp is function f return t is begin return n; end function; end package body; entity e is generic(g : integer := 8); end entity; architecture a of e is package pi is new work.gp generic map(integer, g); package pv is new work.gp generic map(bit_vector, bit_vector'("101")); use pi.all; use pv.all; constant ci : integer := f; constant cv : bit_vector := f; begin end architecture;
```

## Example 255 Local uninstantiated package, multiple local package instantiation

```
generic(g : integer := 8); end entity; architecture a of e is package lp is generic(type t; n : t); function f return t; end package; package body lp is function f return t is begin return n; end function; end package body; package pi is new lp generic map(integer, g);
```

```
entity e is
```

<!-- image -->

```
package pv is new lp generic map(bit_vector, bit_vector'("101")); use pi.all; use pv.all; constant ci : integer := f; constant cv : bit_vector := f; begin end architecture;
```

## Example 256 Local global uninstantiated package, multiple local package instantiation

```
package gp is package lp is generic(type t; n : t); function f return t; end package; end package; package body gp is package body lp is function f return t is begin return n; end function; end package body; end package body; entity e is generic(g : integer := 8); end entity; architecture a of e is use work.gp.lp; package pi is new lp generic map(integer, g); package pv is new lp generic map(bit_vector, bit_vector'("101")); use pi.all; use pv.all; constant ci : integer := f; constant cv : bit_vector := f; begin end architecture;
```

## Limitation

The following is the limitation of the VHDL 2008 Local Packages feature:

- The VHDL 2008 Local Packages feature is not supported for Coverage, Debug, Xprop, NLP, and Verdi.

<!-- image -->

## Support for Unconstrained Elements in Generics and Generic Types

VCS supports unconstrained elements in the types associated with the formal generic types in VHDL 2008 using the -vhdl08 option.

VCS supports the unconstrained elements for the formal generic types where the arbitrarily complex derived types can be created and used via implicit subtypes, allocators, and aggregates. You must maintain agreement between the element subtypes and the composite subtypes in which they appear, directly or indirectly.

## Example 257

```
package gp is generic (type t); type lh; type alh is access lh; type lt is record l : string; v : t; end record; type vlt is array (natural range <>) of lt; type lh is record n : alh; v : lt; end record; procedure push(l : inout alh; v : t; lbl : string); function dup(v : t; n : positive) return vlt; end gp; package body gp is procedure push(l : inout alh; v : t; lbl : string) is variable e : alh; begin e := new lh'(l, (lbl, v)); l := e; end push; function dup(v: t; n : positive) return vlt is constant k : lt := (to_string(n), v); begin if n = 1 then return (0 => k); else return dup(v, n - 1) & k; end if; end dup; end gp; package pt is
```

```
type bvv is array (natural range <>) of bit_vector; type r1 is record e1 : string; e2 : bvv; end record; end pt; use work.pt.all; package sp is new gp generic map (r1);
```

## Limitations

The Unconstrained Elements in Generics and Generic Types feature has the following limitations:

- The port associations at the VHDL/Verilog boundary is not supported.
- The formal sub element association and the type conversions are not supported.
- The Unconstrained Elements in Generics and Generic Types feature is not supported for Coverage, Debug, Xprop, NLP, and Verdi.
- The array aggregates where the element type is a generic type associated with the unconstrained elements are not supported.

## Support for Connecting VHDL Records to the SV Packed Structs

You can connect VHDL records to SV packed structs by instantiating mixed design or sva\_bind to the VHDL design unit.

This feature is also applied to the following complex types:

- Arrays of arrays
- Multidimensional Arrays (MDA)
- Nested structs and records
- Packed (1-dimensional and multidimensional) arrays of structs and records

The VHDL record definition must match the SV packed struct definition, that is all the fields of the SV packed struct must have one-to-one valid mapping to the corresponding VHDL record members. These connections apply only to the input and output ports.

<!-- image -->

## User Interface

To enable the relaxation of the packed structs for the cross boundary, the following setting is to be applied in the synopsys\_sim.setup file:

```
----------------------------------------------------------------- Elaboration Settings ----------------------------------------------------------------- Relaxes the use of SystemVerilog arrays and structs on the -- language boundary MX_RELAX_ARRAYS_STRUCTS = TRUE
```

This also enables the following setting used to handle the packed arrays on the Mixed Language Design boundary:

```
----------------------------------------------------------------- Elaboration Settings ----------------------------------------------------------------- Relaxes the use of SystemVerilog packed arrays on the -- language boundary MX_RELAX_PACKED_ARRAYS = TRUE
```

## System Verilog Packed Structs

The packed structs in SystemVerilog can only contain packed data types and integer types. The packed data types are the single bit data types (bit, logic, reg), packed arrays of the single bit data types, enumerated types, and recursively other packed arrays and packed structures.

A packed array refers to the dimensions mentioned before the variable or the object name. For example,

```
· reg [5:0] array; · bit [2:0][3:0] array;
```

An unpacked array refers to the dimensions mentioned after the variable or the object name. For example,

```
· reg arr [3:0]; · int arr [2:0][3:0];
```

An unpacked array or an array with packed and unpacked dimensions is not allowed as the packed struct member.

## Note:

The 4-state data type, time , is not supported for this solution; however, it is allowed in a packed structure.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The underlying data type of an enumeration type is int or an anonymous int as specified in the following example:

```
enum {red, yellow, green} light; // anonymous int type enum integer {IDLE, XX='x, S1='b01, S2 ='b10} state; // integer enumeration type
```

The integer types with predefined widths, such as byte , shortint , int , longint , and integer , must not have packed array dimensions declared.

The following is an example of a complex packed struct:

```
bit [4:0] elem1; // 2-state 1-dimensional packed array logic [3:0][4:0] elem2;  // 4-state, 2-dimensional packed array shortint elem3;  // 2-state myenumtype elem4; mystructtype_2 [1:0] elem5;  // packed array of packed structs
```

```
typedef struct packed { } mystructtype_1; with typedef enum { red, yellow, green} myenumtype; and typedef struct packed { logic elem1; } mystructtype_2;
```

## Note:

You cannot define the dimensions of the struct array elements by parameters.

SystemVerilog supports the concept of packed unions, however, VHDL does not support this concept, so the mapping is not possible.

## VHDL records

The VHDL records can contain the following valid VHDL datatypes:

- 2-state and 4-state bit types, such as bit , bit-vector , std\_logic , std\_logic\_vector
- Integer types
- Enumeration types
- Array types. These can be 1-dimensional arrays, but also N-dimensional arrays.
- Records (nested records)

In VHDL, N-dimensional arrays can be defined as follows:

- Multi-dimensional arrays, such as
- type my\_array is array(0 to 1, 3 downto 0) of std\_logic
- Array-of-array, such as
- type my\_array1 is array(7 downto 0) of bit;
- type my\_array2 is array(1 downto 0) of my\_array1;

The following is an example of a complex VHDL record:

```
Type my_record_type is record Member1 : bit; Member2 : std_logic_vector(3 downto 0); Member3 : my_array_type_1; Member4: my_record_type_1; Member5: my_enum_type_1; End record my_record_type; with type my_array_type_1 is array (3 downto 0) of std_logic_vector(7 downto 0); type my_record_type_1 is record member1: std_ulogic; end record my_record_type_1; type my_enum_type_1 is (green, yellow, red, white);
```

## Note:

All the data types of the VHDL record members are constrained and cannot be defined by generics.

## Arrays of Records

The port types can be packed arrays of records or structs. The arrays can have multiple dimensions which can be defined by parameters or generics, as shown in the following example:

```
type record_type is record member1 : std_logic_vector(1 downto 0); end record; type record_array is array (integer range <>) of record_type; and typedef struct packed { logic [1:0] elem1; } struct_type;
```

<!-- image -->

## Instantiated in the following way:

```
module vlog_top(); parameter integer P1 = 1; struct_type [0:P1] struct_var; Design1 #(P1) design1(struct_var);
```

## Note:

Arrays with unpacked dimensions and/or arrays with packed and unpacked dimensions of the packed structs are not supported.

## Mapping Verilog / VHDL types

The mapping of the struct/record port types are defined by the default mappings of each struct member combined with a mapping of the complete struct.

You must create and maintain the struct member with the following conditions:

- The data types of each struct member must be compatible. For example, a Verilog 4state shortint can be mapped upon a VHDL std\_logic\_vector(15 down to 0) type, and not upon a VHDL integer type.
- The number of bits for the representation of each struct member must match with that of the other struct member that includes the array dimensions and the number of array dimensions.
- The number, order, and types of the struct members must match.

The following error messages are displayed for a bit\_vector size mismatch for a struct member:

```
Error-[PCWM] Port connection width mismatch vlog.v, 7 "vhdl_leaf H(ina, outx);" The following 9-bit expression is connected to 6-bit port "SIG2" of module "vhdl_leaf", instance "H". Expression: outx Instantiated module defined at: "vhdl.vhd", 8 Use +lint=PCWM for more details. and/or: Error-[SVABIND_ERROR] SVA-Bind error port and the formal port of type 'VLOG_TYPE_4' do not match. This is because of size mismatch between the record element 'ELEM_0' of size '9' mapped to the packed structure element 'MEMBER_0' of size '6'.  :   bind vhdl_top vlog_leaf V( .ina (sig1),  .outx (sig2)); file:"vlog.v:21"
```

```
SVA-Bind error :     Record size mismatch:The data types of the actual and/or:
```

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

```
Error-[ANALTYPESTRCTREC] Record size mismatch simv.daidir/scsim.db.dir/dummyVhConfig.vhd, 2 DUMMY_MHDL_CFG_VHDL_TOP Line 2.6: Please generate .lis file by 'vhdlan -list ...' and see details. --+   port map (INA => INA, OUTX => OUTX) The data types of the actual port and the formal port of type 'VLOG_TYPE_4' do not match. This is because of size mismatch between the record element 'ELEM_0' of size '9' mapped to the packed structure element 'MEMBER_0' of size '6'. Please map fixed width packed structure elements to record elements of identical sizes. The following error messages are displayed for a bit_vector size mismatch for the unpacked structs: Error-[SVUSTRU-PBOUND-NA] SV unpacked struct not supported vlog.v, 3 VLOG_MIDDLE, "ina" Port "ina" of module "VLOG_MIDDLE" is of SystemVerilog unpacked struct type. SystemVerilog unpacked structs are not allowed across the language boundary. and/or: Error-[SV-NYI-SPMX] Unsupported SystemVerilog feature vlog.v, 5 Unpacked structs are not yet supported across MX boundary: "outx" is of struct type "vlog_type_3". Expression: outx A possible work around is to create a boundary port for each member of the struct. While mapping a 2-state Verilog int to a VHDL natural, writing a negative value from Verilog to the VHDL port results in the following error messages: Error-[SIMERR_CONSTERR_INDEXEDRANGE] Range Violation Error vhdl.vhd, 117 sig3_2.member_1 <= sig2.member_1 + 1; Value -796973059 is out of range 0 to 2147483647 at 18000 PS from process /VHDL_TOP/PROC_CHECK_1. Please extend the range in the type/subtype definition or ensure that the value is within the defined range. The error message is generated when the port is updated with a negative value and the value of the port is used in an expression, such as the 'add' statement.
```

## Examples

Consider the following type of definitions for VHDL and Verilog for the connections:

```
VHDL: subtype vhdl_type_1 is std_logic_vector(3 downto 0); type vhdl_type_2 is (green, yellow, red, blue, purple, black, white); subtype vhdl_type_3 is bit; type vhdl_type_4 is array(1 downto 0, 2 downto 0) of vhdl_type_3; subtype vhdl_type_5 is bit_vector(7 downto 0); type vhdl_type_6 is record Member_0 : vhdl_type_1; -- 4-state vector Member_1 : vhdl_type_2; -- enum (32-bit integer) Member_2 : vhdl_type_4; MDA of bit 2-state Member_3 : vhdl_type_5; -- 2-state vector end record vhdl_type_6; maps to Verilog: typedef logic [3:0] vlog_type_1; typedef enum {green, yellow, red, blue, purple, black, white} vlog_type_2; typedef bit vlog_type_3; typedef vlog_type_3 [1:0][2:0] vlog_type_4; typedef byte vlog_type_5; typedef struct packed { vlog_type_1 elem_0; // 4-state vector vlog_type_2 elem_1; // enum (32-bit integer) vlog_type_4 elem_2; // packed array 2-dims of bit (2-state) vlog_type_5 elem_3; // 2-state 8-bit } vlog_type_6;
```

These types can be used as port types for the Mixed Language Design connections. To use these types for the Mixed Language Design connections, the setting in synopsys\_sim.setup must be applied at the analysis and elaboration phases.

## Verilog-on-top Scenario

Instantiate the following VHDL entity in Verilog using the default flow:

```
VHDL: entity vhdl_dut is port ( p1 : in vhdl_type_6; p2 : out vhdl_type_6 ); end entity vhdl_dut; Verilog: module vlog_top; vlog_type_6 sig1; vlog_type_6 sig2;
```

<!-- image -->

```
vhdl_dut H(sig1, sig2); . . . endmodule
```

This can be analyzed and elaborated according to the following default 3-step flow:

```
vhdlan vhdl.vhd . . . vlogan vlog.v . . . vcs vlog_top . . .
```

## VHDL-on-top Scenario

The same types can be used for a VHDL-on-top/Verilog-down scenario. For all scenarios, instantiate the following Verilog module:

```
Verilog: module vlog_dut(p1, p2); input vlog_type_6 p1; output vlog_type_6 p2; . . . endmodule
```

## Component Instantiation

Consider the following example with the component instantiation where a declaration is made of the Verilog module that is to be instantiated:

```
VHDL: entity vhdl_top is end entity vhdl_top; architecture vhdl_top_arch is signal sig1 : vhdl_type_6; signal sig2 : vhdl_type_6; component vlog_dut is port ( p1 : in vhdl_type_6; p2 : out vhdl_type_6 ); end component vlog_dut; begin V : vlog_dut port map (p1 => sig1, p2 => sig2); . . . end architecture vhdl_top_arch;
```

The actual bindings get resolved during elaboration.

## Direct Instantiation

In direct instantiation, the Verilog module is not declared beforehand, however it is taken directly from the work directory. This implies that the Verilog module is analyzed before the VHDL entity is analyzed:

```
VHDL: entity vhdl_top is
```

<!-- image -->

```
end entity vhdl_top; architecture vhdl_top_arch is signal sig1 : vhdl_type_6; signal sig2 : vhdl_type_6; begin V : entity work.vlog_dut port map (p1 => sig1, p2 => sig2); . . . end architecture vhdl_top_arch;
```

## Instantiation by Means of sva\_bind

With the SVA bind construct, a Verilog module can be instantiated within a VHDL scope without changing the VHDL code. This requires the 'bind' instruction inside a Verilog file, and the bind option for the elaboration.

The following example has bind instruction inside a Verilog file:

```
Verilog: module vlog_bind; bind vhdl_top vlog_dut Vbind(.p1(sig1), .p2(sig2)); endmodule
```

The Verilog file is normally analyzed with vlogan , and the complete design is elaborated with the following option to enable the sva\_bind feature:

```
vcs vhdl_top -sva_bind_enable vlog_bind . . .
```

## Limitations

The Connecting VHDL Records to the SV Packed Structs feature has the following limitations:

- In SystemVerilog, all types are packed types and a packed struct in SystemVerilog can only contain other packed members, integer types, and single bit types.
- In SystemVerilog packed structs, the concept of packed unions is not supported in VHDL which results in no mapping.
- In the array of records, arrays with unpacked dimensions and/or arrays with packed and unpacked dimensions of the packed structs are not supported.
- The vhdlan analysis option, -gen\_sv\_pkg , generates a SystemVerilog package according to the VHDL package definition. However, it does not generate a SystemVerilog package for the packed structs and the packed arrays. Therefore, the generated packages cannot be used for the Mixed Language Design connections.
- Connections with the packed structs to the VHDL records are not supported for the INOUT ports.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Mapping a SystemVerilog (Nested) Packed Struct to a VHDL Vector Type

SystemVerliog packed structures can be mapped to the VHDL vector types and vice versa, only if both the sides contain the same number of bits.

The supported SystemVerilog packed structures are as follows:

- Scalar and 1-D vector fields
- Packed structures and nested packed structures
- Packed array of packed structures
- Packed arrays and multidimensional packed arrays

The supported VHDL vector types are as follows:

- bit\_vector : a 2-state vector type.
- std\_logic\_vector : a 9-state vector type, that matches to the Verilog 4-state logic type.

## Use Model

To enable the mapping a SystemVerilog (nested) packed struct to a VHDL vector type feature,

- Use the following commands:
- Set the MX\_RELAX\_ARRAYS\_STRUCTS variable to TRUE in the synopsys\_sim.setup file.

```
vlogan -sverilog <file_name> vhdlan -vhdl08 <file_name> vcs <top_name> -R
```

## Example

Consider the following example demonstrating the mapping of a SystemVerilog (nested) packed struct to a VHDL vector type feature:

```
Test.v typedef struct packed { logic [3:0] elem_1; bit [1:0] elem_2; logic elem_3; } str; module vlog_leaf(input str data_in, output str data_out); assign data_out = data_in; initial $monitor("data_out = %0b", data_out); endmodule
```

```
Top.vhd library ieee; use ieee.std_logic_1164.all; entity top is end entity; architecture behav of top is subtype vhdl_vector is std_logic_vector(6 downto 0); signal sig1, sig2 : vhdl_vector; component vlog_leaf is port ( data_in : in vhdl_vector; data_out : out vhdl_vector); end component vlog_leaf; begin process begin sig1 <= "1010101"; wait for 1 ns; wait; end process;
```

```
V : vlog_leaf port map (data_in => sig1, data_out => sig2); end architecture; Run the test cases with the following commands: vlogan -sverilog Test.v vhdlan -vhdl08 Top.vhd vcs top -R The following output is generated: data_out = 1010101
```

## Limitations

The following are the limitations of mapping the SystemVerilog (nested) packed struct to VHDL vector type feature:

- The inout ports of the packed struct are not supported.
- The Verilog packed structs with an enumeration typed member and the packed union members are not supported.

## VHDL Unconstrained Generic Formal Sub Element Association

VCS supports the VHDL unconstrained generic Formal Sub Element Association (FSA).

## Example 258 Legacy Unconstrained Array

```
entity e is generic(g : bit_vector);
```

<!-- image -->

```
end e; architecture a of e is begin end a; entity top is end top; architecture a of top is begin
```

<!-- image -->

```
u1 : entity work.e generic map (g(0) => '1', g(1) => '0'); end a; Example 259 VHDL 2008 Unconstrained Element Type package p is type r is record f1 : bit_vector; f2 : string; end record; end p; use work.p.all; entity e is generic(g : r); end e; architecture a of e is begin end a; entity top is end top; architecture a of top is begin u1 : entity work.e generic map (g.f2 => "ab", g.f1 => "10"); u2 : entity work.e generic map (g.f2 => "ab", g.f1(0) => '1', g.f1(1) => '0'); u3 : entity work.e generic map (g.f1(0) => '1', g.f1(1) => '0', g.f2 => "ab"); u4 : entity work.e generic map (g.f1(0) => '1', g.f2 => "ab", g.f1(1) => '0'); u5 : entity work.e generic map (g.f1(0) => '1', g.f2(1) => 'a', g.f1(1) => '0', g.f2(2) => 'b'); end a;
```

## Limitation

The VHDL unconstrained generic FSA feature is not supported for multidimensional arrays FSA.

## VHDL 2008 Generics in Subprograms

VCS is enhanced to support the VHDL 2008 LRM generics in subprograms feature. For a VHDL 2008 feature, you must use the vhdlan -vhdl08 option.

You can enable the VHDL 2008 generics in subprograms feature using one of the following methods:

- Use the vhdlan -Xgens\_in\_subp option.
- Set the GENS\_IN\_SUBP environment variable as True in the synopsys\_sim.setup file.

The following example shows how you can supply a data type in a generic map:

## Example 260 VHDL 2008 Generics in Subprograms

```
package p is function eq generic (type t) parameter (x, y : t) return boolean; end p; package body p is function eq generic (type t) parameter (x, y : t) return boolean is begin return x = y; end function; end p; use work.p.all; entity e is end e; architecture a of e is signal b : bit; signal n : natural; signal v : bit_vector(1 to 4) := "1011"; procedure eqg generic (type t) parameter(x, y : t) is begin assert x = y; end procedure;
```

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## You can instantiate the procedure and function to get versions for various types in the following way:

```
procedure eqpb is new eqg generic map(bit); function eqfb is new eq generic map(bit); procedure eqpn is new eqg generic map(natural); function eqfn is new eq generic map(natural); procedure eqpv is new eqg generic map(bit_vector(1 to 4)); function eqfv is new eq generic map(bit_vector(1 to 4));
```

The eqpb and eqfb identifiers are the names of the subprogram instances; and the generic map supplies actual generics for the formal generics defined by the uninstantiated subprogram. If all the formal generics have default values, you can omit the generic map implying the use of default values. After instantiating the subprogram, you can use the instance name to call the instance.

```
begin eqpb(b, '0'); assert eqfb(b, '0'); eqpn(n, 0); assert eqfn(n, 0); eqpv(v, "1011"); assert eqfv(v, "1011"); end a;
```

## Limitation

The VHDL 2008 Generics in Subprograms feature is not supported in the KDB, Coverage, and Xprop flows.

## VHDL 2008 Record Type Conversions

With VHDL 2008, you can declare records with the elements of the unbounded array types, which can be constrained later when declaring objects, interfaces, subtypes, and more. This feature ensures that the record type conversions validate the bounds of the operand against the target subtype.

The subtype validations applied to the record type conversions must be the same as the ones applied in assignments, subprogram calls, and so on. The VHDL 2008 Record Type Conversions feature supports conversions to fully constrained record type or subtype.

## Use Model

To enable the VHDL 2008 record type conversions feature, use the -vhdl08 compile option with vhdlan , as follows:

```
vhdlan -vhdl08 <file_name>
```

## Example

The following example demonstrates the use of unconstrained and constrained types in VHDL, specifically focusing on records, arrays, and subtypes:

```
package p is type bvv is array (natural range <>) of bit_vector; type mdab is array (natural range <>, natural range <>) of bit; type ur is record e0 : bit_vector; e1 : bvv; e2 : mdab; end record; end p; package body p is end p; use work.p.all; entity leaf is generic (g : ur); end leaf; architecture a of leaf is constant k1 : ur := g; begin end a; use work.p.all; entity top is end top; architecture a of top is component leaf generic (g : ur); end component; constant k1 : ur := (X"AA", (X"A", X"B", X"C", X"D"), (X"0", X"1", X"2", X"3")); subtype t1 is k1'subtype; -- fully constrained, different bounds, same sizes subtype tfc is ur (e0 (107 downto 100), e1 (104 downto 101)(50 to 53), e2 (53 downto 50, 33 downto 30)); begin t : process begin
```

<!-- image -->

```
end process; i1 : leaf generic map (k1); i2 : leaf generic map (tfc(k1)); end a;
```

## Limitations

The VHDL 2008 record type conversions feature has the following limitations:

- The partially constrained array subtypes are not supported.
- Type conversions to a record subtype with unconstrained elements are not supported.

## VHDL 2008 Use Clauses

VHDL 2008 supports the use clauses for type declarations feature. This feature ensures that all the predefined operations and any overloaded declarations of the predefined operations in the same scope are visible.

The following is the supported list of features:

## Predefined operations

- Logical operations: and or nand nor xor xnor (binary and unary) · Comparison: =, /=, &lt;, &lt;=, &gt;, &gt;=, ?=, ?/=, ?&lt;, ?&lt;=, ?&gt;, ?&gt;=, ?? · Shift and rotate: sll, srl, sla, sra, rol, ror · Arithmetic operations: + -(binary and unary), &amp; , * / mod rem , ** abs not · Reduction: minimum, maximum · String conversion: to\_string · File operations: file\_open, file\_close, read, write, endfile, read, write (unconstrained), file\_open (with status)
- deallocate

## On declarations

- Types and subtypes
- Scalar (enumeration (character type), integer, floating-point, physical)
- Composite (Array, Record)

<!-- image -->

- Access
- File
- Aliases of all the types and sub types

## Use Model

To enable the VHDL 2008 use clauses feature,

```
· Use the -vhdl08 compile option with vhdlan , as follows: vhdlan -vhdl08 <file_name> · Set the VHDL2008_USE_CLAUSE variable to TRUE in the synopsys_sim.setup file.
```

## Example

The following example demonstrates the use of custom types, overloaded operators, and assertions in VHDL:

```
package pack is type color_type is (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, violet); function "<" ( c1, c2 : color_type ) return boolean; type color_vector is array (natural range <>) of color_type; type bv is array (natural range <>) of bit; end stuff; entity top is end top; architecture a of top is begin proc_1 : process use work.pack.color_type; use work.pack.color_vector; use work.pack.bv; constant k1 : bv := "10101010"; constant k2 : bv := "11001100"; constant k3 : color_vector := (red, blue, yellow, red); constant k4 : color_vector := (red, blue, yellow, green); begin assert (k1 xnor k2) = "10011001"; wait; end process; end a;
```

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## VHDL 2019 Conditional Analysis Tool Directives

Conditional analysis tool directives are supported by VCS. For more information on conditional analysis, refer to section 24.2 in the VHDL 2019 LRM.

This feature enables you to control which part of the description to use during the Analysis phase. The conditional\_analysis\_directive are as follows:

```
`if conditional_analysis_expression then 'elsif conditional_analysis_expression then `else `end [ if ] `warning string_literal `error string_literal
```

For more information about using the directives, see the IEEE Std. VHDL 2019 LRM .

## Use Model

Conditional analysis tool directives are supported with the following options:

```
-vhdl87 , -vhdl93 , -vhdl02 or -vhdl08 (vhdlan) options. OR VHDL_MODE = vhdl87 , VHDL_MODE = vhdl93 , VHDL_MODE = vhdl08 or VHDL_MODE = vhdl02 setup variable.
```

## Usage Example

Consider the following example:

## Example 261 t1.vhd

```

## VHDL 2019 LRM: Signal and Variable Constrained by Initial Value

VCS leverages the existing solution for the constants constrained by the initial value and applies it to the signals and variables. The Signal and Variable Constrained by Initial Value feature is a VHDL 2019 feature, so you must use the -vhdl19 option.

<!-- image -->

## Consider the following test case, test.vhd :

----test.vhd---library IEEE; use ieee.std_logic_1164.all; use ieee.numeric_std.all; entity e is end e; architecture a of e is function f1 return string is variable v1 : string := "abcd" & "EF"; begin return v1; end f1; signal s1 : string := f1; signal s2 : signed := "011" - 1; begin p: process variable v1 : string := f1; variable v2 : signed := "011" - 1; begin wait for 2 ns; v1 := "FEdcba"; v2  := "111"; wait; end process p; end a; Compile test.vhd using the following commands: % vhdlan -vhdl19 test.vhd % vcs e -debug_acc+r Run simulation using the following command: % simv -ucli -i command_file The following is the content of the command_file file: senv time show -val s* show -val p/v* run 4 ns senv time show -val p/v* quit
```

## VHDL 2019: Support for Conditional Expressions

Starting with this release, VCS supports conditional expressions as specified in the VHDL 2019 Language Reference Model (LRM). The 2019 LRM takes the conditional syntax similar to the one used in the conditional variable assignment statements. It allows the conditional syntax in a place where the expression might be used, either directly in cases where it has no significant impact on the grammar, or enclosed in parentheses elsewhere.

Conditional expressions can simplify declarations and expressions, such as declarations for temporary values, or functions encapsulating an if statement, which might otherwise require additional declarations. It is beneficial when the conditional expressions are available in your designs or when you require them for incorporating IP.

To support conditional expressions, you must invoke the vhdlan command with the -vhdl19 switch.

If the VHDL\_MODE setup variable is set to 19 or VHDL19 , VCS enables the VHDL 2019 constructs and the other supported values.

VCS supports conditional expressions at the following places:

- actual designator
- attribute specification
- constant declaration
- variable declaration
- signal declaration

<!-- image -->

- interface object declaration (static)
- statements (including unaffected )
- variable assignment
- force
- value return
- elsewhere (enclosed in parentheses)

```
For example, h1 : filter(a, b, x * 10 when c < 5 else x * 20 when c < 10 else x * 100); attribute filter_length of a : architecture is x * 10 when c < 5 else x * 20 when c < 10 else x * 100; constant flen : integer := x * 10 when c < 5 else x * 20 when c < 10 else x * 100; function get_flen (base : integer; bmul : integer := x * 10 when c < 5 else x * 20 when c < 10 else x * 100) return integer; function get_flen(x, c : integer) return integer is variable i : natural; v begin return x * -3 when c < 0 else unaffected; for i in 0 to 100 loop return x * b when i >= c; -- implicit else unaffected b := a + b; a := b - a; i := i + 1; end loop; -- error if b < a is false, function returns without value return 0 when b < a; end get_flen; procedure report_flen(v : integer) is begin return when v < 0; report "filter length = " & to_string(v); end report_flen; v := 3 * (x * 10 when c < 5 else x * 20 when c < 10 else x * 100); -- error, result expressions must be the same type v := x * 10.0 when c < 5 else x * 20 when c < 10 else x * 100 ns; -- error, conditional expression must be enclosed in parentheses
```

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

```
v := ('0', '0', '0' when c < 5 else 'L' when c < 10 else '1'); -- error, no else clause at end of expression v := (others => ('X' when c < 0 else '0' when c < 5 else 'L' when c < 10));
```

## The following are the error messages for the conditional expressions:

```
Error-[ANL-CONDE-MUE] Missing unconditional expression errmue.vhd, 12 A ("null array" when a'length = 0 else ^ A conditional expression must have a final unconditional expression. Add a final unconditional expression. Error-[ANL-CONDE-NA] Conditional expression not allowed errno19.vhd, 8 A constant k : integer := 5 when g < 5 else 10 when g < 7 else 6; ^ Conditional expressions are not allowed when analyzing as VHDL 2008 or earlier. Analyze with -vhdl19 to enable VHDL 2019 features. Error-[ANL-CONDE-UNA] Unaffected not allowed erruna.vhd, 13 A unaffected when a'length = 1 else ^ A conditional expression may not evaluate to unaffected. Replace uses of unaffected with value expressions.
```

## 27

## SAIF Support

The Synopsys Power Compiler enables you to perform power analysis and power optimization for your designs by entering the power command at the vcs prompt. This command outputs Switching Activity Interchange Format (SAIF) files for your design.

SAIF files support signals and ports for monitoring as well as constructs such as generates, enumerated types, and integers.

This chapter covers the following topics:

- Using SAIF Files with VCS
- SAIF System Tasks for Verilog or Verilog-Top Designs
- The Flows to Generate a Backward SAIF File
- SAIF Calls That Can Be Used on VHDL or VHDL-Top Designs
- SAIF Support for Two-Dimensional Memories in v2k Designs
- UCLI SAIF Dumping
- Criteria for Choosing Signals for SAIF Dumping
- Improving Simulation Time by Reducing the Overhead due to SAIF File Dumping

## Using SAIF Files with VCS

VCS has native SAIF support so you no longer need to specify any compile-time options to use SAIF files. If you want to switch to the old flow of dumping SAIF files with the PLI, you can continue to give the option -P $VPOWER\_TAB $VPOWER\_LIB to VCS, and the flow will not use the native support.

Note the following when using VCS native support for SAIF files:

- VCS does not need any additional switches.
- VCS does not need a Power Compiler specific tab file (and the corresponding library)
- VCS does not need any additional settings.
- Functionality is built into VCS.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## SAIF System Tasks for Verilog or Verilog-Top Designs

This section describes SAIF system tasks that you can use at the command line prompt.

Note that mixedHdlScope in the following discussion can be one of the following:

- Verilog scope
- VHDL scope
- Mixed HDL scope

Note also that a design\_object in the following discussion can be one of the following:

- Verilog scope or variable
- VHDL scope or variable
- Any mixed HDL scope or variable

```
$set_toggle_region
```

Specifies a module instance (or scope) for which VCS records switching activity in the generated SAIF file. Syntax:

```
$set_toggle_region( instance [, instance ]); $toggle_start
```

Instructs VCS to start monitoring switching activity.

## Syntax:

```
$toggle_start(); $toggle_stop
```

Instructs VCS to stop monitoring switching activity.

## Syntax

```
$toggle_stop(); $toggle_reset
```

Sets the toggle counter to 0 for all the nets in the current toggle region.

## Syntax:

```
$toggle_reset(); $toggle_report
```

Reports switching activity to an output file.

## Syntax:

```
$toggle_report("outputFile", synthesisTimeUnit, mixedHdlScope);
```

This task has a slight change in native SAIF implementation compared to PLI-based implementation. VCS considers only the arguments specified here for processing. Other arguments have no meaning.

VCS does not report signals in modules defined under the 'celldefine compiler directive.

```
$read_lib_saif
```

Allows you to read in a state dependent and path dependent (SDPD) library forward SAIF file. It registers the state and path dependent information on the scope. It also monitors the internal nets of the design.

## Syntax:

```
$read_lib_saif("inputFile"); $set_ga l v moni r $set_gate_level_monitoring
```

Allows you to turn on or off the monitoring of nets in the design.

## Syntax:

```
$set_gate_level_monitoring("on" | "rtl_on");
```

The "on" and "rtl\_on" keyword arguments are called policies.

"rtl\_on" Monitors all reg, tri, and trireg data objects for toggles. Monitors other types of nets for toggles if they are cell highconn (ports that connect toward the top of the design hierarchy in a module declared to be a cell).

"on" Monitors all net type of objects for toggles. Monitors reg data objects if they are cell highconn. This is the default monitoring policy.

Verilog memories, Multi-dimensional arrays, and SystemVerilog data objects are supported with an extended syntax:

```
$set_gate_level_monitoring("on" | "rtl_on", "mda" | "sv");
```

You include the mda argument for Verilog memories and multi-dimensional arrays, the sv argument for SystemVerilog data objects.

For more details on these task calls, refer to the Power Compiler User Guide .

<!-- image -->

## Note:

```
The $read_mpm_saif , $toggle_set , and $toggle_count tasks in the PLIbased vpower.tab file are obsolete and no longer supported. on : Monitors both ports and signals. off : Does not print ports or signals. rtl_on : Monitors both ports and signals (same as on) <region/signal> Arguments for specifying the following: region : Mixed HDL/VHDL region and its children to consider for monitoring. signal : (hierarchical path to) signal name. Note: VHDL variables are not dumped in SAIF SDPD (VHDL gate level). Examples # power -enable
```

```
# power -report
```

## The Flows to Generate a Backward SAIF File

You can generate the following kinds of backward (or output) SAIF files:

- an SDPD backward SAIF file - using a library forward (or input) SAIF file
- a non-SDPD backward SAIF file - without using a library forward (or input) SAIF file.

## Generating an SDPD Backward SAIF File

To generate an SDPD backward SAIF file, include the SAIF system tasks in the module definition containing the $read\_lib s f $read\_lib\_saif("inputFile") system task.

## For example:

```
initial begin $read_lib_saif(" inputFile "); $set_toggle_region( mixedHdlScope ); // initialization of Verilog signals M $toggle_start; // testbench M $toggle_stop;
```

<!-- image -->

```
$toggle_report("outputFile", timeUnit,mixedHdlScope); end
```

The $set\_ og l r i n $set\_toggle\_region(mixedHdlScope) system task's scope argument must be one level higher in the design hierarchy than the scope of the module in the library forward SAIF file, for which you intend VCS to generate the backward SAIF file.

For example, if VCS monitors instance top.u\_dut.u\_saif\_module , the argument to the

```
$set_toggle_region system task is top.u_dut , as follows: $set_toggle_region(top.u_dut);
```

Enclose the modules listed in the library forward SAIF file, those from which you intend VCS to monitor and generate the backward SAIF file, between 'celldefine and 'endcelldefine compiler directives.

## Generating a Non-SPDP Backward SAIF File

If you are not including a library forward (or input) SAIF file, include the $set\_gate\_level\_monitoring("on") system task with the other SAIF system tasks.

## For example:

```
initial begin $set_gate_level_monitoring("on"); $set_toggle_region( mixedHdlScope ); // initialization of Verilog signals, and then: $toggle_start; // testbench M $toggle_stop; $toggle_report("outputFile", timeUnit, mixedHdlScope ); end
```

## SAIF Calls That Can Be Used on VHDL or VHDL-Top Designs

VHDL use model mainly consists of the power command and its options at the simv command-line.

The power command syntax is as follows:

```
power -enable -disable -reset -report <filename> <synthesisTimeUnit> <mixedHdlScope> <filename> [<testbench_path_name>] -gate_level on|off| rtl_on <region/signal/variable>
```

## Here:

-enable: Enables monitoring of switching (toggle\_start).

<!-- image -->

```
-disable : Disables monitoring of switching (toggle_stop). -reset : Resets monitoring of switching (toggle_reset). -report : Reports switching activity to an output file (toggle_report). -gate_level : Turns on or off the monitoring based on the following:
```

- on : Monitors both ports and signals.
- off : Does not print ports or signals.
- rtl\_on : Monitors both ports and signals (same as on)

&lt;region/signal&gt; : Arguments for specifying the following:

- region : Mixed HDL/VHDL region and its children to consider for monitoring.
- signal : (hierarchical path to) signal name.

## Note:

VHDL variables are not dumped in SAIF SDPD (VHDL gate level).

## Examples :

```
# power -enable # power -report
```

## SAIF Support for Two-Dimensional Memories in v2k Designs

SAIF supports monitoring of two-dimensional memories in v2k designs.

You must pass the mda keyword to the $set\_gate\_level\_monitoring system task to monitor two-dimensional memories in v2k designs.

If you want to dump through the UCLI command, you must pass the mda string to the power -gate\_level command, as shown in the below section.

## UCLI SAIF Dumping

The following is the use model for UCLI SAIF dumping:

```
% simv -ucli ucli% power -gate_level on mda ucli% power <scope> ucli% power -enable ucli% run 100 ucli% power -disable ucli% power -report <saif_filename> <timeUnit> <modulename> ucli% quit
```

<!-- image -->

## Criteria for Choosing Signals for SAIF Dumping

## Verilog :

VCS supports only scalar wire and reg, as well as vector wire and reg, for monitoring. It does not consider wire/reg declared within functions, tasks and named blocks for dumping. Also, it does not support bit selects and part selects as arguments to $set\_toggle\_region or $toggle\_report . In addition, it monitors cell highconns based on the policy.

## VHDL :

Signals or ports are supported for monitoring. Variables are not supported, as it is difficult to infer latches/flops at RTL level.

Constructs like generates, enumerated types, records, array of arrays integers, and so on, are also supported over and above the basic VHDL types.

The following rules are followed regarding the monitoring policy for VHDL:

```
Port  Signals  Variables on       Y      Y       N off      N      N       N rtl_on   Y      Y       N
```

## Mixed HDL :

The rules for mixed HDL are basically the same as that of VHDL if VHDL is on top, and Verilog if Verilog is on top.

## Improving Simulation Time by Reducing the Overhead due to SAIF File Dumping

SAIF file dumping is enhanced to improve the simulation time by reducing the overhead due to SAIF.

## Use Model

At runtime, you can use the -saif\_opt -saif\_opt option with appropriate arguments to reduce the overhead due to SAIF file dumping as shown in the following command line:

```
% simv [simv_options] -saif_opt+option1+option2+...
```

You can specify one or more options along with the -saif\_opt option. The options available are as follows:

```
tog le_s ar i n toggle_start_at_set_region
```

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

```
Use this option to implicitly call $toggle_start with $set_toggle_region . tog le_s p a r toggle_stop_at_toggle_report Use this option to implicitly call $toggle_stop with $toggle_report . skip_cel d f n o skip_celldefine_scopes
```

Use this option to skip monitoring activity for the modules that are defined under the `celldefine compiler directive or are resolved using -v and -y options.

## Example

## Consider the following example:

```
`timescale 1ns/1ns module top; wire w; bot b(w); initial begin #5 $set_gate_level_monitoring("rtl_on"); $set_toggle_region(b); #95 $toggle_stop; $toggle_report("1.saif", 1e-9, b); $finish; end endmodule module bot(output reg p); initial begin #20 p = 1'b1; #20 p = 1'b0; #20 p = 1'b1; #20 p = 1'b0; end endmodule To run the example, use the following commands: % vcs -sverilog 1.v % simv -saif_opt+toggle_start_at_set_region It generates the following output: /** The set_gate_level_monitoring command explicitly turns ON the
```

```
internal nets monitoring **/ (SAIFILE (SAIFVERSION "2.0") (DIRECTION "backward") (DESIGN) (VENDOR "Synopsys, Inc") (VERSION "1.0")
```

```
(DIVIDER / ) (TIMESCALE 1 ns) (DURATION 95.00) (INSTANCE top (INSTANCE b (NET (p (T0 40) (T1 40) (TX 15) (TC 3) (IG 0) ) ) ) ) )
```

## Limitations

The feature has the following limitations:

- The skip\_celldefine\_scopes option is supported only if library forward SAIF file is not read.
- The enhancements are not supported for UCLI power command.
